title: TV-L E13 PhD Pay in Germany: Contract Percentage, Gross Pay and Benefits
seoTitle: TV-L E13 PhD Salary: Percentage, Steps and Gross Pay
seoDescription: Understand a German TV-L E13 PhD offer by checking the pay group, step, contract percentage and applicable table before estimating take-home pay.
intro: TV-L E13 describes a pay group, not a single PhD take-home salary. Your contract percentage, pay step and deductions determine what the advertised figure means for your budget.
description:
TV-L E13 describes a pay group, not a single PhD take-home salary. Your contract percentage, pay step and deductions determine what the advertised figure means for your budget.

Read the percentage and pay step

An E13 vacancy should state the applicable collective agreement and contract percentage. A part-time percentage applies to the relevant full-time gross rate; it does not describe your take-home income. The pay step can depend on recognised experience and the employer assessment.

Ask for an individual payroll estimate

Confirm the current pay table, contracted hours, appointment dates and expected step with the employer. Income tax and mandatory contributions affect net pay. Avoid treating another researcher paycheck as your own estimate, particularly when personal circumstances or contract terms differ.

Compare the full appointment

Check leave, insurance arrangements, pension contributions, research duties and extension conditions in the contract. Ask how doctoral supervision and registration relate to employment. Budget using a confirmed estimate and local housing costs, then allow for moving expenses before your first salary payment.

Read the contract line by line

A vacancy quoting E13 still needs a contract percentage, pay step and applicable agreement to become a usable salary estimate. Ask which previous experience can be recognised and whether the employer can provide an indicative payroll calculation. Do not multiply another person’s net income by your contract percentage: deductions do not necessarily behave that way. Record the gross rate separately from estimated take-home pay and benefits. Confirm the working hours, appointment period and doctoral duties so that the financial offer and the research commitment are understood together.

E13 is a pay group, not a take-home amount

A German doctoral advert may show several pieces of information in one line: the pay agreement, the pay group, the contract percentage and the appointment period. Read all of them. E13 identifies a pay group within the named agreement. It does not establish that every doctoral researcher receives a full-time salary or the same net payment.

TV-L and TVöD are different agreements, and other arrangements can apply. Use the agreement named by the employer. For a TV-L offer, consult the employer's current table or the official TdL material and check the date on which the table takes effect. An anticipated start date in a later year is a reason to ask which published rate applies, not to invent a future salary.

How the calculation works

ElementWhat it meansWhat you should confirm
Pay groupClassification such as E13The agreement and group written into the contract.
StepPosition within the pay group's progressionWhich prior experience is recognised and the starting step.
Contract percentageShare of the relevant full-time appointmentContracted hours and the salary fraction actually paid.
Effective datePeriod covered by the pay tableThe table applicable when employment begins.
DeductionsAmounts affecting take-home payAn estimate based on your own circumstances.

Here is an arithmetic example using an invented full-time base solely to explain the percentage. If the full-time gross base were €4,000 per month, a 50% appointment would give €2,000 gross, 65% would give €2,600, and 75% would give €3,000. These are not current E13 rates and must not be used as an offer estimate. Actual allowances, payroll rules and deductions require the employer's calculation.

Contracted time and doctoral work

Ask what the funded duties are and how they connect with the doctorate. Teaching, project delivery, laboratory support and independent thesis work can be arranged differently between appointments. A salary percentage is not, by itself, a full explanation of the research workload. Discuss expectations with the supervisor and check the employment documents with HR.

Read the appointment's start and end dates alongside the doctoral registration arrangements. A fixed-term employment contract and the academic permission to pursue a doctorate are related but separate. If the research plan extends beyond the guaranteed contract period, ask what support is confirmed and what remains a future application. Record a possible extension as possible until it is awarded.

Build a budget from an individual estimate

For housing decisions, use a payroll estimate relevant to your circumstances rather than a general gross-to-net percentage. Keep ordinary monthly income separate from irregular payments. Add rent, utilities, insurance arrangements, transport and the costs of moving. If you are relocating with family, use the needs of that household rather than a single-person example from another city.

A useful HR enquiry includes the vacancy reference, expected starting date, proposed contract percentage and the experience you want assessed for the initial step. Ask which documents are needed. This gives HR the information to answer without requiring you to interpret every payroll rule yourself.

Is a scholarship paid under TV-L?

A scholarship is not automatically an employment contract under TV-L. Read the award terms and compare payment, insurance, leave and other conditions separately.

Can two E13 doctoral offers pay different amounts?

Yes. Contract percentage, starting step, applicable dates and individual deductions can differ. Compare the complete appointment before deciding which offer provides a workable income.

Read the appointment period alongside the project plan

A grant's overall duration does not necessarily equal the length of your employment contract. Check the dates in the offer and ask how they relate to the planned thesis work. If an extension is mentioned, distinguish a confirmed commitment from a possibility dependent on review or further funding. Ask how recognised experience affects the starting step and which evidence HR needs to assess it. Keep the answer with the salary estimate, particularly if the proposed start date changes. Comparing these details can reveal a meaningful difference between two offers that use the same pay-group label. Use the confirmed contract for financial planning and keep future support in a separate, conditional note.

Keep the payroll estimate with its date and the assumptions used.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • TdL: TV-L agreement and official tables
  • DAAD: doctoral finance
